front: Explain the mental model of MCP Client (how the system thinks).
back: An MCP client (Cursor, Claude Desktop, custom SDK host) connects to one or more MCP servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts over a transport. The LLM never talks to your server directly — the client mediates capability discovery and tool calls.

front: Symptom: Server not listed in Cursor — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: MCP settings → logs; JSON syntax · Fix: Fix mcp.json; restart Cursor

front: Symptom: needsAuth / 401 — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Server status; OAuth flow · Fix: Run mcp_auth; refresh token

front: Symptom: Tool call hangs — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Server stderr; backend connectivity · Fix: Timeout; fix DB URL / VPN

front: Symptom: command not found — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: which npx; PATH in GUI app · Fix: Absolute path to node/npx in config

front: Symptom: Empty tool list — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Server startup crash on import · Fix: Run command manually; fix env vars

front: Symptom: Works in CLI, not Cursor — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Cursor inherits different env · Fix: Put secrets in env block, not shell profile

front: Symptom: Protocol version error — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Client vs server version skew · Fix: Update server package or pin version

front: Gotcha with MCP Client: what silently fails?
back: Secrets in args — connection strings in mcp.json sit on disk. Prefer env vars; never commit tokens.

front: When should you NOT use MCP Client?
back: Simple static docs — link the doc; don't wrap in MCP. High-QPS automation — use direct API/SDK; MCP adds LLM mediation overhead. Untrusted servers — MCP server runs with host privileges; audit before adding.

front: What is MCP (Model Context Protocol) in one sentence?
back: Open protocol for AI clients to discover and call tools, read resources, and exchange prompts with servers — USB-C for LLM integrations.

front: Explain the mental model of MCP (Model Context Protocol) (how the system thinks).
back: An MCP host (Cursor, Claude Desktop) runs MCP clients that connect to MCP servers over stdio, SSE, or streamable HTTP. Servers expose tools (functions), resources (readable URIs), and prompts. The model requests a tool call; the client executes it on the server and returns structured results.

front: Symptom: Server not listed — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Config JSON syntax · Fix: Validate; restart host

front: Symptom: Tool call timeout — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Server logs · Fix: Increase timeout; fix blocking I/O

front: Symptom: Auth errors (remote) — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: OAuth/API key · Fix: mcp_auth flow in host; rotate creds

front: Symptom: Schema mismatch — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: Tool input schema · Fix: Align server tool definition with client expectations

front: Symptom: stdio garbled output — what do you check and fix?
back: Check: println debug on stdout · Fix: Log to stderr only in MCP servers

front: Gotcha with MCP (Model Context Protocol): what silently fails?
back: MCP server = arbitrary code execution — only install trusted servers; review tool permissions. Secrets in server env — same discipline as CI secrets; don't log tool args with tokens. Spec drift — pin server version; hosts update faster than servers.

front: When should you NOT use MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
back: Don't build MCP for a one-off script you'd run once in terminal — shell script is simpler. Don't expose production DB write tools without authz layer and audit logging.
